messages:
Maria: heads-up — BigCorp asked for an extended deprecation bridge when we swap their pinned model; they want a 90-day soft-compat period + traffic shadowing. any objections?
Kevin: 90 days sounds long for infra cost, but we can do a graduated taper (90 -> 60 -> 30) with auto-rollbacks if error rates spike.
Julie: can we scope this as a customer-exception lane rather than changing the default pin policy? want to avoid precedent.
Dave: BigCorp will push hard on the 90d, they have legal asks. if we make it an exception, they still expect migration support (benchmarks + runbook).
Kevin: proposed technical plan:
```
- create exception flag on tenant config
- enable shadowing for N requests (configurable %)
- add perf/breakage evals from their golden prompt set
- schedule canary cutover with auto-fallback to pinned model
```
Maria: +1. what are launch gates? specifically what benchmarks do we need to accept the swap?
Julie: need pass on: 1) latency < +30% p95, 2) quality regression < 2% on their eval set, 3) no data exfil windows. if shadowing shows steady regressions we delay.
Kevin: ops notes: shadowing incurs KV cache pressure; recommend limiting to 10% traffic initially. Also we'll need a dedicated canary pool for their heavy prompts.
Dave: customer will provide the golden prompt set and 3 labeled priority intents. they want a weekly sync during the 1st month.
catalog-bot: Policy link updated: https://redwood.infra/policy/deprecation-exceptions (v1.2)
Maria: ok action items: Kevin -> prototype exception flag + shadowing config (ETA 2w). Julie -> draft customer-risk agreement + gating checklist. Dave -> collect prompt set and share by EOD Friday. I'll owner the rollout plan and comms.
Kevin: noted. I'll add an infra cost estimate to the ticket. cc @eng-runtime for kernel/kv concerns.
Julie: can we schedule a quick 30m with legal to confirm contract language for 90/60/30 taper?
Dave: I'll set up the customer sync invite after we have the draft runbook.
Maria: thanks team :thumbsup: we'll reconvene after the prototype. If infra cost looks prohibitive propose fallback: shorter soft-bridge + migration credits to customer.
Kevin: understood — will call out cost vs risk in the PRD.
Julie: +1 on migration credits as a compensating control.
Maria: closing thread for now — follow-ups in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4821
